tips.en: Heavy, painful periods can have more than one cause. A clinician usually uses an ultrasound or scan to tell them apart.

How is it different from endometriosis
How is adenomyosis found
Does it get better after menopause
Does it affect pregnancy

redFlags.symptom: Bleeding so heavy that protection is soaked every hour or two
redFlags.quote: need to change your pad or tampon every 1 to 2 hours

redFlags.symptom: Severe pain during periods
redFlags.quote: you have severe pain during your periods

name: Vaginal and pelvic health (BV, yeast, UTI)
aiJobs: Log: itch, odour, discharge change and burning in her words, kept discreet
Insights: how many episodes she has noted in 6 and 12 months, as counts
Visit prep: timeline of symptoms and how many times they recurred, with her questions
Ask: explain how these three differ and when to be seen, education only
covered: log_phrases.dart discharge words (watery, creamy, sticky, eggWhite), bladderUrgency
safety.dart urgent phrases
gaps: No terms for itch, odour, fishy smell, burning urine, so the intimate-symptom log cannot be built and the assistant cannot count episodes
No discreet mode behaviour in assistant output (neutral wording on a shared screen); vocabulary has vaginalDryness flagged elevated only
No UTI red-flag words (fever, back or side pain, blood in urine) in safety.dart
No recurrence rule and no visit question for repeated infections

visitQuestions.en: I keep getting the same discharge or urine symptoms. How can we find the cause and stop them coming back?
visitQuestions.when: Three or more symptom notes of the same kind in 12 months

visitQuestions.en: My urine symptoms keep returning. Should I have a urine test?
visitQuestions.when: Bladder terms logged on 3 or more days in 2 separate months

tips.en: Douching and scented washes can upset the natural balance of the vagina.
tips.trigger: A discharge, itch or odour note is logged

tips.en: If you think you have a urine infection, it is important to see your doctor.
tips.trigger: Bladder urgency logged on 2 or more days in a week

askTopics: How do BV, yeast and UTI differ
Why do these keep coming back
Is vaginal discharge normal
What helps prevent recurrence (education only)
When to see a doctor about urine symptoms

redFlags.symptom: Fever or pain in back or side with urine symptoms
redFlags.quote: Pain in your back or side below the ribs

redFlags.symptom: Urine or vaginal symptoms during pregnancy

name: Sexual and reproductive health (STI awareness, HPV bridge)
aiJobs: Ask: answer STI and testing questions from CDC, NHS and WHO pages, as education and 'talk to a clinician'
Learn: bridge to cervical-screening and HPV guides
Visit prep: a private list of concerns she finds hard to say aloud
Safety: no verdicts, no 'safe', no contraception advice
covered: trusted_sources.dart includes cdc.gov, nhs.uk, who.int so cloud answers on STIs are grounded
safety.dart birthControl fixed sentence
guide_search.dart for HPV and screening guides
gaps: Conservative register (MR-47): no sexual-wellness logging, so the optional test log in the spec should stay out; the assistant needs an explicit rule to answer clinically and to decline details beyond education
Ask has no discreet-answer behaviour for shared screens
No visit question about testing or HPV vaccination status and cervical screening dates
safety.dart birthControl fires on partner or protection questions with a fixed sentence only, which can feel like a dismissal for an STI question

tips.en: Many infections cause no symptoms, so feeling well does not rule one out. A clinician can explain which tests suit you.
tips.trigger: A guide on STIs is opened

askTopics: What are common STIs and their symptoms
Why get tested if I feel fine
What does a test involve
How does HPV link to cervical screening
What should I do if a partner tells me they have an STI

name: Sexual wellbeing (pain, low desire)
aiJobs: Ask: explain pain with sex, dryness and low desire as clinical topics from ACOG and NICE pages, with 'who to see' routing
Visit prep: a discreet page of the clinical symptoms she chose to log and her questions
Insights: counts of painDuringSex and vaginalDryness days only, nothing else
Safety: no desire scoring, no technique or dilator advice
covered: log_vocabulary.g.dart has libidoUp, libidoDown, vaginalDryness, painDuringSex as elevated terms (hidden on shared screens)
visit_summary.dart excludes elevated terms from the summary list
log_phrases.dart has no phrases for these terms, by design (OD-5)

No 'what kind of clinician' route in Ask
No postpartum or menopause-linked routing for dryness or pain
